title: Ferdinand II to Garcilaso de la Vega, 31 Aug 1498: the head line and ten-line postscript in Garcilaso's cipher (ACA Sástago 193, nº 79/83; DECODE R10180)

documents.shelfmark: Barcelona, ACA, Diversos, Sástago 193 (Lío B), nº 79/83; DECODE R10180; Parisi 2004 doc. 83

plaintext.source: none for the Garcilaso-cipher passages; the body (Escrivà cipher no. 2) is printed in Parisi 2004 pp. 105-109

transcription.source: DECODE images IMG_R10180_I46659_P4 (ten lines) and P5 (head line), 2x line crops
transcription.notes: The measure counts 3 [gap] lacuna markers: 315 sign tokens, 79 types (57 with superscript variants folded). Water stains in L1 and L3-L4; several base signs are close in shape.

system.summary: Homophonic symbol alphabet with letter+superscript code groups (aᵠ, eᵗ, bⁿ) and capital-letter name signs, distinct from the Escrivà ciphers used in the body of the letter.
system.notes: The seven commonest signs cover 40% of tokens. Every key in BRAH 9/15 (DECODE R9815-R9832, R9486), Escrivà nos. 1-2 and the Cifra general was compared and excluded. Garcilaso's own cipher survives in deciphered letters at RAH Salazar A-11, not digitised.

prior_solution.where: Parisi 2004 printed the body and left both passages undeciphered; Tomokiyo, Cryptoole IT1498-1 and DECODE list them as open

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code, and posed the problem with /goal and the catalogue page solve/349. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: solve.py (homophonic annealer, 5-gram Spanish model with Parisi's 1495-98 texts)

solution.what: Fetched the seven R10180 images from DECODE with the session cookie; located the two passages (P5 head line, P4 last ten lines) against Parisi's notes 13, 71, 89.

Parisi 2004 (UB mirror), Tomokiyo unsolved.htm/spanish.htm and blog, Cryptoole, DECODE siblings R10172-R10179, Villanueva Morte and Fernández de Córdova 2025: no reading anywhere; key specimens cited at RAH Salazar A-11 ff. 109-111 and 121-125, not online.

Found Galende's BRAH 9/15 key file on DECODE (R9815-R9832, R9486) and compared every alphabet with the postscript signs, including the Alonso de Silva-Garcilaso cipher (R9822) and the f. 16 Rome cipher (R9824).
Compared Parisi's Escrivà alphabets 1 and 2, the Cifra general (esp318) and RAH 9/7-9/8 cipher letters on DECODE (R9483-R9485, R9591).
Transcribed both passages sign by sign from 2x crops into ct.txt (12 rows).
Counts, repeats (π bong zh, ꝑ π, aꝛaꝛ), contact variety; superscripted letter pairs identified as probable code groups, capitals as name signs.
Place-and-date crib 'en Çaragoça a' on the last tokens before the clear date.
Homophonic annealer, one letter per sign type, 5-gram Spanish (es-golden-age + Parisi texts), unigram KL penalty; full and folded sign sets.
Same annealer on 315 letters of es-gutenberg Spanish under a 57-symbol homophonic key: 0-29% of letters recovered in six restarts.

outcome.method_basis: Both passages were transcribed and attacked ciphertext-only and against every reachable key; no key fits, and a control shows 315 homophonic tokens are below what the annealer can break.
outcome.notes: Needs RAH Salazar A-11 ff. 109-111 and 121-125 (Garcilaso's cipher letters with decipherments) to rebuild the key.

credits.note: located the passages and named the RAH A-11 Garcilaso cipher letters as the probable key (Pedralbes 24, 2004, n. 13)
